mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a single month signals a strengthening demand for housing, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with persistent inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% annually and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable, it signals strong economic growth without inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows > 2% annually and CPIAUCSL stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between GDPC1 growth and stable CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
